statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode)
statistics.quote: We confirmed these observations by analysis of variance (ANOVA) for the adaptation phase, using the between-factor Age and the within-factor Episode: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
statistics.direction_quote: Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects. ... An exponential fit yielded y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young subjects and y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old subjects.
statistics.admissible_reason: Between-subjects main effect of Age on pointing error across the 15 adaptation episodes (the perturbation block containing the late-adaptation window); no separate late-episode contrast is reported.
statistics.notes: This is the overall Age main effect for the whole adaptation phase, not a contrast restricted to the final adaptation episode.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Episode main effect
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant factor (Episode), not a between-group comparison.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the adaptation phase — Age × Episode interaction
statistics.quote: significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term, not a group mean contrast.

statistics.quote: Accordingly, ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.admissible_reason: Different phase: refresh phase after the five-minute break, not the initial perturbation (adaptation) block.

statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01) and Episode (F(2,44)=6.18, P<0.01), but no significant interaction.
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant factor and a different phase.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26
statistics.quote: we compared the pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 by an additional ANOVA; the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction, in accordance with the view that the initial reduction was not age-dependent.
statistics.admissible_reason: Collapses the last adaptation episode (20) with a refresh-phase episode (26); not a test of the late-adaptation window alone.
statistics.notes: Episode 20 is the final adaptation episode, but this ANOVA averages it with episode 26 of the refresh phase.

statistics.locator: Results, additional ANOVA comparing pointing errors in episodes 20 and 26 — Episode effect
statistics.quote: the effects of Age (F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) and Episode (F(1,22)=7.79, P<0.05) were significant but not their interaction

statistics.notes: These pages report only F and t statistics with P levels, exponential fit parameters (y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young; y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old), and Fig. 1 means/SDs; no Cohen's d, Hedges' g or eta-squared is given.

parsed.notes: No per-episode or late-adaptation-specific between-group contrast is reported; the closest admissible statistic is the between-subjects Age main effect for the whole 15-episode adaptation phase, F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05. Direction (old subjects showing larger pointing errors / less adaptive improvement) is supported by 'adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects' and the exponential-fit asymptotes (9.92 deg young vs 29.51 deg old). Other tests on these pages concern different outcomes and are not transcribed here: the after-effect phase ANOVA (Episode F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001; interaction F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01), the tracking-transfer ANOVA (Procedure F(1,43)=144.09, P<0.001), and the trail-making test t(22)=5.25, P<0.001.
